correctness.rationale: For any shore z with sum Z, the opposite open sums are Z−z_i. An all-negative shore is infeasible, so each sum is ≥2 and is ≥3 if the shore has a 2. A sum 2 means no 2, an even shore size n≥4, and at least one −1. Its opponent needs a 2 to defend this −1 and cannot itself contain −1; its sum is then ≥n+1, so the two sums cannot total ≤6. Hence total weight ≥6 and equality requires sums (3,3). At sums (3,3) every open sum is automatically ≥1. Two 2s per shore at odd n, or a shared unique 2 index at even n, give the stated feasible constructions. The two linear equations give a,b in terms of c. For odd n≥5, c is even and c=0 would leave at least one −1 on that shore; the opponent then must have no −1, impossible at sum 3 on n>3 vertices. At n=3, both all-1 or both with two 2s yield 1+3² configurations, and mixed cases fail. For even n, c is odd; if both c≥3 there are S_n² pairs. If one c=1, a fixed index of its 2 must avoid the other shore's negatives, giving the T_n(c)(n−a_n(c))/n factor and both orientations. If each has one 2, fix the first shore. The second 2 is at the same index with C(n−1,a_1) choices of negatives, or at one of the first shore's b_1 label-1 positions, in which case two indices are forbidden to second-shore negatives and there are C(n−2,a_1) choices. This establishes the entire count without relying on finite extension. Separate exhaustive replay through n=8 agrees with each of the six counts and finds only (3,3) among minimizing shore-sum pairs.
residual_risks: Independent finite exhaustion stops at n=8. Larger n, classification and exact counts depend on the symbolic argument, not on the frozen formula evaluations through n=40.

originality.rationale: The uniformly quantified crown result and parity census are distinct from the inspected general graph results; no standalone novelty is credited for small cases those results cover. The cycle determination cited by Koster et al. covers Cr_3=C6. For Cr_4, their cubic theorem gives weight 8−2=6 and their equality proof also gives the count 84 by choosing a maximum open packing and its defenders. The cubic and cycle results do not cover n≥5. Complete bipartite and ≥3-part complete multipartite formulas do not apply after deleting the matching. The same-day ordinary total Roman census has different labels and constraints. The broader crown theorem and census pass subject to the stated retrieval limits.
residual_risks: The edge-modification paper and the Zhao–Miao full text were unavailable in the inspected routes. Some broader equivalent result may be unindexed or stated differently; search is not proof of priority.

value.rationale: The crown is a canonical single-perfect-matching modification of complete bipartite graphs. The uniform law compares its exact domination weight to the very different unmodified case, while the all-order extremizer structure and count quantify how the missing matching affects optimal labelings. The parity split and the interaction of unique defenders provide meaningful census information beyond the already implied small-order values.
residual_risks: Does not treat arbitrary matching deletions or enumerate nonminimum signed total Roman functions.
